title: Architect flows
summary: Flow types, tasks, in-queue experiences, data actions, bots, secure calls, and publish.

lessons.title: The flow types on the Architect home page
lessons.summary: Architect is a list of flow types. Picking the wrong tab is the first defect.
paras: The home page documents inbound call, inbound message, inbound email, inbound chat, outbound call, bot flow, common module, in-queue call, in-queue email, in-queue message, secure call, voicemail, workflow, and survey invite. The create-a-flow article also names digital bot flows, voice survey, web survey invite, and workitem flows. Names must be unique inside one type, may repeat across types, and may be at most 200 characters.

You need Architect flow permissions to add, edit, and view, plus the routing permissions the flow type requires. Message and email flows ask for an error-event queue. A new flow can take a few seconds to appear. The home page has a refresh for that lag. It is not a failed save.

lessons.title: Tasks, menus, and a way out
lessons.summary: An inbound call flow plays audio, collects input, and must transfer, hand off, or disconnect.
paras: About Architect describes linking actions: play audio, route to agents, queues, voicemail, numbers, or other flows, collect digits outside a menu, dip data, and branch with expressions. The inbound example in the bot article shows a question, a decision, and a transfer. That shape is the whole product in miniature.

A flow with only Play Audio has no exit. Transfer to ACD needs a real queue. Disconnect needs a reason the caller can understand. Call Bot Flow is an exit only if the bot itself has a failure path back to a queue. Secure flows are a special case covered later. They use a blind transfer rather than a consultation VXML transfer.

lessons.title: In-queue flows are the hold experience
lessons.summary: The caller is already queued. The in-queue flow is what they hear or read while ACD looks for an agent.
paras: For calls, Architect supplies a default in-queue flow built around a music action. Menus and reusable tasks are not available in that flow type. The default is not published for you. Until you publish it, it does not handle waiting calls. You can replace the music and add actions, then republish.

Email and message do not get a built-in default. You create those in-queue flows and attach them. An outbound email or message does not launch the in-queue flow. It launches when an inbound response arrives. Treat any exact overall timeout you remember as something to re-read on the in-queue article. The page describes those periods and they are easy to mis-quote.
lessons.uncertainty: The in-queue article also describes overall and recurring periods for email and message flows. Re-read those numbers on the page rather than trusting a remembered duration.

lessons.title: Data actions and participant data
lessons.summary: A data action calls a system outside the flow. Participant data carries a value to the agent.
paras: Architect’s own description includes data dips and expressions. A Call Data Action is how a flow asks Salesforce, a REST service, or another connector for an answer and then branches. Set Participant Data is how a later agent, script, or screen pop sees what the flow learned. The Salesforce and Zendesk articles both describe screen pop and interaction logging as the agent-facing end of that story.

The action fails closed when the credential is wrong. Salesforce username-password credentials for data actions are on a deprecation path. The migration guide says to use the Salesforce OAuth client-credentials credential: consumer key, consumer secret, and My Domain URL. No change to the request body is required for that credential swap. A flow that worked last year can fail on auth alone.

lessons.title: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks
lessons.summary: A common module is a flow type you call from other flows. The name is still unique inside that type.
paras: The Architect home page lists common module as its own type so you can build logic once and reuse it across flow types. The 200 character name limit and the per-type uniqueness rule still apply. A module that transfers to a queue hard-codes that queue unless you pass the queue in. Passing the queue in is the difference between a library and a copy.

Reusable tasks inside a single flow are not the same object as a common module shared by many flows. In-queue call flows, notably, do not offer reusable tasks. If the hold experience needs shared logic, you are in a different design conversation than a common module called from an inbound flow.

lessons.title: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
lessons.summary: A secure flow is how a caller enters a card number without that audio being recorded or shown to the agent.
paras: The Architect home page describes secure call flows as the way to stop system recording and agent access while a caller enters sensitive digits, such as a payment. The create article says these flows are either agent-initiated or started by another call flow, and that Genesys uses a blind transfer rather than a consultation VXML transfer so the transfer does not fail.

This is not the same control as a queue recording policy. Recording policies decide which ACD calls are recorded at all. A secure flow is a hole in that recording for a segment. You still design the return path to the agent, and you still do not log the digits into participant data “for the screen pop.” That would undo the point.

lessons.title: Call a bot from the inbound flow
lessons.summary: Dialog Engine bot flows and digital bot flows are Architect flow types. The inbound flow calls them. It does not become them.
paras: Genesys documents Dialog Engine Bot Flows for voice and digital flows, and Digital Bot Flows for message experiences. The inbound article shows creating a bot, asking a question, and calling that bot from the inbound flow. Intents come back as outcomes the flow can branch on. A banking template in that article checks a balance or finds a branch.

Call Bot Flow and Call Digital Bot Flow are different actions for different bot types. An external bot connector is a third action family. The connector list changes. Confirm the current connector in Architect rather than designing around a vendor this lab does not have an open product page for. Always give the bot a failure output that transfers to a queue.

lessons.title: Publish, division, and Flow Insights
lessons.summary: A saved flow is a draft. The runtime uses the published version. Insights tell you whether anyone hit it.
paras: Create, edit, and publish are different moments. In-queue flows make that obvious because the default exists and still does nothing until publish. The same discipline applies to inbound flows, bots, and common modules. Flow Insights, referenced from the bot documentation, shows how often pieces of a flow run. A flow that Insights says never runs is usually a routing problem: the call route, the queue’s in-queue selection, or the bot call is pointing somewhere else.

The flow’s division controls who can edit it. An admin in the wrong division will swear the flow is missing. It is not missing. Their role is not granted on that division. Fix the grant or move the flow. Do not create a second copy under a new name and leave the published one in place.
